clue.text: Militant has incomplete view on start of play

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the piece it sits on

parts.note: a play starts with Act I, its first act

indicators.note: incomplete says the word for view loses its final letter here

parts.note: a vista is a view

explanation.surface: A firebrand rates a play badly after seeing only its opening scenes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of play' is Act I, the opening act, not a single letter; 'incomplete' trims the last letter of the view word, and 'on' places it after.
explanation.definitionFit: An activist is a campaigner, someone militant in pursuit of a cause.

clue.text: Cat he twice confused — a wild one

indicators.note: confused says the letters of cat and the doubled he are jumbled together
twice says the word he is used two times in the pool of letters

explanation.surface: A muddled cat, or a muddled man, meets a wild animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' gives HEHE, and 'confused' rearranges CAT plus HEHE.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheetah is a wild member of the cat family, so it is a wild cat, the 'one' standing for the clue's cat.

clue.text: Decoration of golf club an affliction to be borne

parts.note: an iron is a type of golf club
a cross to bear is a burden or affliction one must endure

explanation.surface: A golfer regards a club as a heavy burden to carry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iron Cross is a German military medal, an honour awarded for bravery.

clue.text: Fashionable attempt to accept a new post here

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: to accept says the word for attempt takes another letter inside it

parts.note: a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A stylish effort to take on a new job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accept' puts A inside TRY to give TRAY.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-tray is the desk tray where incoming mail is placed awaiting attention.

clue.text: Collins novel description of Irene Adler's wedding?

explanation.surface: A literary question about a Holmes character's bridal outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: Wilkie Collins wrote the novel; Sherlock Holmes always called Irene Adler 'the woman', and a bride wears white.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of Wilkie Collins's 1859 mystery, and also a playful picture of Holmes's 'the woman' dressed as a bride.

clue.text: Blend of claret for political alliance

indicators.note: blend of says the letters of the wine word are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Wine is blended to serve a political coalition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartel is a combination of parties or firms acting together, an alliance.

clue.text: Company at Magdalene used to add flavour to ale

definitions.text: used to add flavour to ale

parts.note: Mary Magdalene is St Mary in church naming

explanation.surface: A college company at Magdalene brews ale with a flavouring.
explanation.walkthrough: Magdalene reads like the Oxford or Cambridge college but stands for St Mary Magdalene.
explanation.definitionFit: Costmary is a herb, also called alecost, once used to flavour beer.

clue.text: Pain in poor rat's wind-pipe

indicators.note: in says the word for pain goes inside the scrambled rodent
poor says the letters of rat are in bad shape and rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: A sick rat has a sore windpipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' signals the rodent's letters are scrambled, and 'in' puts the pain inside them; 'wind-pipe' is the definition, not a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The trachea is the tube carrying air to the lungs, the windpipe.

clue.text: Mere versifiers?

parts.note: mere is an old word for a lake, so these are poets of the lakes rather than mere rhymesters

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark about mediocre poets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mere' looks like 'only'; it is a lake, pointing to Wordsworth, Coleridge and Southey of the Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: Wordsworth, Coleridge and Southey lived by the English lakes, the region where a mere is a lake.

clue.text: Story nobody wants to hear in magazine

definitions.text: nobody wants to hear in magazine

explanation.surface: Some news is unwelcome at a magazine office.
explanation.walkthrough: The magazine is an ammunition store, where the bang of a gun or explosion is the last thing anyone wants.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is an account or story, and also the loud bang of a gunshot or explosion.

clue.text: Soft touch of midshipman, note

parts.note: Mr Midshipman Easy is the hero of Captain Marryat's naval novel
a mark is a note, as in to mark or note something

explanation.surface: A young naval officer's gentle tap is noted.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Midshipman Easy is an 1836 novel by Frederick Marryat.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy mark is a gullible person, someone easily taken advantage of.

clue.text: Manner of playing — musical turns about to follow

indicators.note: turns says the musical's title is read backwards

parts.note: Cats is the famous Lloyd Webber musical
CA, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A performer's style follows the twists of a show tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reverses the Lloyd Webber show's title; 'about' is the Latin circa, abbreviated as in dates.
explanation.definitionFit: Staccato is a way of playing notes short and detached.

clue.text: MP without his constituents — a piece of bad luck

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside says the two letters wrap around the rest
constituents says the letters of his are rearranged, as parts making up a whole

explanation.surface: An MP has lost the voters of his seat, an unlucky turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituents' looks like voters but signals a rearrangement of the pronoun; 'without' is used in its old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishap is an unlucky accident, a minor misfortune.

clue.text: A change for one in Greek isle spells confusion

indicators.note: change for says one letter of the island is swapped out for another

parts.note: Chios is a Greek island in the Aegean
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A shift for someone on a Greek island is confusing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A change for one' swaps the I of CHIOS for A.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaos is utter disorder, complete confusion.

clue.text: Authority for enclosure? There's no equity in it

definitions.text: Authority for enclosure? There's no equity in it

parts.words: Authority for enclosure? There's no equity in it
parts.note: the legal system built on judges' precedent, separate from the rules of equity, and once used to settle rights over shared fields

explanation.surface: A legal puzzle about fencing off land without fairness.
explanation.walkthrough: English law long had two strands: judge-made precedent and equity, a separate fairer system of remedies; enclosure fenced off shared village land.
explanation.definitionFit: Common law is judge-made law based on precedent, historically distinct from equity.

clue.text: Note reality gets distorted in this

definitions.text: Note reality gets distorted in this

parts.note: fa is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: gets distorted says the letters of reality are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark that truth is bent in a certain kind of story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets distorted' rearranges the clue's own word for real life, after the sol-fa note; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairy tale is a story of magic and make-believe, where real life is bent out of shape.

clue.text: Sort of engine required for short rally?

explanation.surface: A question about what engine a quick motor rally needs.
explanation.walkthrough: The rally is a tennis exchange, not a motor race: a short one has only two hits.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-stroke is an engine with a two-phase cycle, and a very short tennis exchange is just two hits.

clue.text: Hire again to top fruit

indicators.note: to top means to cut off the head, so the fruit loses its first letter

parts.note: a greengage is a plum-like fruit

explanation.surface: Someone is re-hired to pick the fruit at the top of the tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to top' means to behead, as with topping a carrot.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-engage someone is to take them on once more, employ them again.

clue.text: State aimed to get revision of papers etc.

parts.note: MASS is the abbreviation for the US state of Massachusetts

indicators.note: get revision of says the letters of aimed are revised into another order

explanation.surface: A state government plans to revise its official documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get revision of' rearranges AIMED into MEDIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The mass media are newspapers, radio and television reaching the public at large.

clue.text: Make more pleasant report about Paris season coming up

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
about says the word for report wraps around the French season

parts.note: news is a report
ete is French for summer

explanation.surface: A story of a Parisian summer approaching makes things nicer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the French summer inside the report word, giving NETEEWS; 'coming up' reads that upwards, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweeten something is to make it more agreeable or attractive.

clue.text: Takes over the game

explanation.surface: Someone seizes control of the match.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bowler bowls an over, a set of six deliveries; bowls is also the lawn game.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricketer bowls an over, delivering its six balls, and bowls is the lawn game with weighted woods.

clue.text: Part of newspaper van

explanation.surface: A newspaper section, or a delivery vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'van' is short for vanguard, those at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaders are editorial articles in a paper, and also those in the van, at the front.

clue.text: What supporters did when delayed?

explanation.surface: Fans did something when their trip was late.
explanation.walkthrough: Supporters here are props or braces, not fans.
explanation.definitionFit: Props bear a weight up, and being delayed means being kept late.

clue.text: Never the same again for a hero .of opera?

definitions.text: Never the same again for a hero .of opera?

parts.words: Never the same again for a hero .of opera?
parts.note: a barroom order of a single measure of a juniper spirit, rather than a repeat, names Tchaikovsky's title hero

explanation.surface: A singer's life is changed for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as ONE GIN, it is a fresh order at the bar rather than 'the same again'; whole, it is Tchaikovsky's Eugene Onegin.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugene Onegin is the title hero of Tchaikovsky's opera after Pushkin.

clue.text: Flier he devoured in conflict

indicators.note: in says the man and his meal go inside the word for conflict

parts.note: a war is a conflict
ate means devoured

explanation.surface: A pilot eats in the middle of a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' suggests a pilot or leaflet, but it is a bird; 'in' puts the man and his meal inside the conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: The wheatear is a small migratory songbird, a bird and so a flier.

clue.text: Wise men from East first guided by light to king at one

parts.note: lit means light, as in a lit room
R is short for rex, Latin for king
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The Magi follow a star from the east to the infant king.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes the Magi; 'first guided by light' puts LIT before E.
explanation.definitionFit: The literati are the learned, educated and literary people of a society.

clue.text: Wooster's club used by pipers

explanation.surface: A gentlemen's club that hires bagpipers.
explanation.walkthrough: Bertie Wooster, of P. G. Wodehouse's stories, belongs to the Drones Club.
explanation.definitionFit: Wodehouse's Bertie Wooster belongs to the Drones Club, and drones are the bagpipe's continuous bass pipes.

clue.text: Nathaniel's at home at the seaside

explanation.surface: A man named Nathaniel lives by the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Nathaniel Winkle is a member of Dickens's Pickwick Club.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Nathaniel Winkle is one of Dickens's Pickwickians, and the periwinkle is a sea snail that lives on rocky shores.

clue.text: Coffee obtained from one's press officer

indicators.note: obtained from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A drink fetched by a publicity aide.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso is strong black coffee made by forcing steam through ground beans.
